correctness.rationale: A polar vertex iff the tight-edge graph is connected; tight spanning trees force integer hub-relative potentials in {-1,0,1}. This gives necessary and sufficient adjacency/sign and zero-support conditions; the explicit four-state automaton counts them without duplication. Centering yields p+q-(p-q)^2/(m+1); a full case analysis bounds all potentials by m-1-epsilon/(m+1), classifies the two/four equality cases for m>=3, and antipodal support inequalities give the global radius. Noncontact strict slack plus the exact rank 1/2 of equality normals yields affine center locus dimension m-1/m-2. The self-contained exact Fraction verifier agrees for m=2..10 and 6846 vertices, including independent finite transfer counts and contact rank. No finite check is being treated as an infinite proof.
